# Computing the Field Extension Degree $[F_{p^2}(t)(t^{1/p}):F_p(t)]$

## Setting Up the Tower

I'll use the **tower law** by introducing the intermediate field $F_{p^2}(t)$:

$$F_p(t) \;\subseteq\; F_{p^2}(t) \;\subseteq\; F_{p^2}(t)(t^{1/p})$$

This gives:

$$[F_{p^2}(t)(t^{1/p}):F_p(t)] = [F_{p^2}(t)(t^{1/p}):F_{p^2}(t)] \cdot [F_{p^2}(t):F_p(t)]$$

## Computing $[F_{p^2}(t):F_p(t)]$

Since $F_{p^2} = F_p(\omega)$ for some element $\omega \in F_{p^2}\setminus F_p$ with $[\!F_{p^2}:F_p\!]=2$, adjoining the transcendental element $t$ to both fields preserves the degree:

$$[F_{p^2}(t):F_p(t)] = [F_{p^2}:F_p] = 2$$

## Computing $[F_{p^2}(t)(t^{1/p}):F_{p^2}(t)]$

The element $t^{1/p}$ is a root of $x^p - t$. In characteristic $p$, we have $x^p - t = (x - t^{1/p})^p$, so this polynomial has at most one distinct root. It is **irreducible** over $F_{p^2}(t)$ if and only if $t$ is **not** a $p$-th power in $F_{p^2}(t)$.

**Checking irreducibility:** Suppose $t = g(t)^p$ for some $g(t) \in F_{p^2}(t)$. Writing $g(t) = \sum_i a_i t^i$, we get:

$$g(t)^p = \sum_i a_i^p \, t^{pi}$$

For this to equal $t$, we would need a term with exponent $1$, but all exponents in $g(t)^p$ are multiples of $p \geq 2$. Contradiction. Hence $t$ is not a $p$-th power in $F_{p^2}(t)$, so $x^p - t$ is irreducible and:

$$[F_{p^2}(t)(t^{1/p}):F_{p^2}(t)] = p$$

## Final Computation

Applying the tower law:

$$[F_{p^2}(t)(t^{1/p}):F_p(t)] = p \cdot 2 = 2p$$

$$\boxed{2p}$$
